plan.notes: Source: official Montana State University 2026-2027 Academic Catalog PDF (https://catalog.montana.edu/pdf/2026-2027.pdf), pp. 153-154, 'B.S. in Computer Science, Professional Option' -- the catalog's genuine term-by-term plan grid (Freshman/Sophomore/Junior/Senior Year, Fall/Spring columns with per-term Year Totals; Total Program Credits: 120). The 2026-2027 catalog is the current edition (not archived). Transcription method: manual transcription of every grid cell (course code, title, credits) on 2026-09-30; per-term sums re-verified against the catalog's printed Year Totals (14/15, 16/16, 15/15, 15/14). Caveats: (a) MSU's B.S. in Computer Science is offered in TWO options -- Professional Option (this plan; capstone CSCI 468 Compilers) and Interdisciplinary Option (p. 154; ESOF 423 capstone + minor). No option-less 'B.S. in Computer Science' exists; the Professional Option is transcribed as the standard track. (b) Catalog rules: minimum 120 credits; 42 credits must be numbered 300 and above; 19 credits from the Upper Division Elective Choices list and 12 credits from the CS or Related Electives Choices list (excess upper-division elective credits may fulfill CS-or-Related credits); detailed requirements on the Professional Option Graduation Worksheet at www.cs.montana.edu/forms.html. (c) The catalog's term grid does not list per-course prerequisites, so prereq arrays are intentionally empty -- no prereqs invented; the published term ordering preserves the prerequisite chain. (d) CSCI 481 Program Assessment is a required 0-credit course (required_zero). (e) The published sequence begins with M 171Q Calculus I in semester 1; students not calculus-ready adjust via advising (not stated in the grid).
